Web search for the Zápolya letters to the Bavarian dukes, Łaski, Augurelio, Acta Tomiciana: no edition

Push-to-95% pass: every unread R9414 word set beside its raw decrypt (decrypt_v2, cp12/dec_*_new) and resolved only where the decrypt itself spells the word: 'Lunden' (P1.34, the Archbishop of Lund, Charles V's negotiator with King John), 'feind' (P3.04), 'befelch' (P2.17), 'handstain' (P4.34, mining term); remaining gaps not supported by the decrypt left unread

Full-resolution re-transcription of every non-code R9414 gap (r9414/pass4.txt); accepted 'ist', 'auch er', 'wut', 'sag wan', 'seiner', 'red'; withdrew 'handstain'; found an unkeyed barred-d sign at five gaps and the Psi code at P1.18/P1.25

Joint LM scoring (de-1500s) of the unkeyed barred-d sign over its five R9414 places, all letters and 23 digraphs/short words, plus the large Psi word sign (proposed 'Mt.'); siblings R9403, R9415, System B key and sperantio1534 checked for both signs

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3869 tokens, 33 types, de-1500s order 4: reading -2.249 per letter; random keys -6.676 (z 6.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.639 (mean -3.69, z 54.4); annealer on the real text -2.399. Verdict: pass.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from kaa4591b (catalogue 162), whose other two letters are in Łaski's System B (R9403, now with the other System B letters in kaa4591b) and system L (R9415, moved to sperantio1534). Profile, validation and measure carried over: they were already R9414's alone.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R9414 linked to the latest sign transcriptions (transcription_p12.txt, transcription_p34.txt), the reading reading_v5.txt and the raw decrypt decrypt_v2.txt; key_file keyb.txt with its alternatives alt_p12.txt

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): r9414/reading_v5.txt read line by line. Most of the letter builds German sentences with single-word holes (reviewed B); the bands P1.12-32, P2.15-19, P3.01-09, P3.39-P4.01, P4.21-35, P5.05-07 break into fragments ([..n] and <...> runs in nearly every clause) and are split off as decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.922 -> 0.648 (words in the lines that read).

Re-read b37 step 1 for the unread bands: DECODE R9414 re-fetched (six images, no attachment); neighbouring records R9408-R9417 checked by record page (System A′, Sperantio, system L, System B letters; none a copy or decipherment of R9414); no edition known.

Scored the unread bands of reading_v5.txt: 0.310 clean sentences (de), 0.379 on explicit holes, against 0.561 / 0.848 for the lines that read; pass4.txt entries re-checked against decrypt_v2.txt for P1.12-16; no value holds across the letter. Bands kept decoded, not read.

texts.summary: An unnamed Bavarian servant at King John's court writes to Duke Ludwig of Bavaria from Wardein (Nagyvárad): his journey back into Hungary, envoys of the pashas of Belgrade and Bosnia, the Sultan arming 'hundert tausent man' to win Hungary and then turn on Austria, the Ferdinandists taking towns; he asks Ludwig to intercede with Duke Wilhelm, and mentions debts, mining and ore specimens.

reading_review.note: Verified 23 Oct 2026 (r2c, VERIFY3_BRIEF): the v3 sweep's 0.419 scored the whole of r9414/reading_v5.txt, bands included (texts[1], decoded, not read). The lines of this entry, written out as r9414/R9414_reading.md (v5 wording unchanged; v5's <doubtful runs> and word? conjectures printed [?...], so they count as holes), score 0.464 plain and 0.71 on explicit holes (v2_score.py, 49 of 69 sentences), hole rate 0.115 (the same lines without paragraph labels: 0.735). Early New High German, so the word list cannot know the spelling and the explicit-hole share is the bar: above it. Read through: the envoys of the pashas of Belgrade and Bosnia, the Sultan's order to arm, his aim to win Hungary and then Austria, the plea to Duke Ludwig to speak to his brother, the closing and date build sentences with single holes. Keeps read. Rests on key r9414/keyb.txt + alternatives, seeded from the interlinear gloss over P1 l.6-8, and four image passes. English: r9414/R9414_en.md.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 89.2% of the words of r9414/R9414_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
